AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND THE OCCUPATIONAL TAX ORDINANCE FOR THE TOWN OF CLERMONT, GEORGIA; TO PROVIDE AND CLARIFY DEFINITIONS UNDER THE ORDINANCE; TO PROVIDE THAT ALL BUSINESSES SHALL BE CLASSIFIED USING THE SAME CRITERION, IN ORDER TO ASSURE UNIFORMITY; TO PROVIDE FOR A NEW TAX SCHEDULE; TO PROVIDE A PENALTY FOR NONPAYMENT OF TAXES WHEN THERE HAS BEEN NO PAYMENT OF TAXES FOR 90 DAYS; TO PROVIDE FOR INTEREST ON ACCRUED AND DELINQUENT OCCUPATIONAL TAXES; TO DELETE SECTION 17 IN ITS ENTIRETY AND TO PROVIDE FOR A NEW SECTION 17 OF SAID ORDINANCE; TO PROVIDE THAT ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE LICENSES ARE NOT COVERED BY THE ORDINANCE; THAT DISABLED VETERANS AND BLIND PERSONS WITH PROOF OF EXEMPTION ARE NOT COVERED BY THE ORDINANCE; TO PROVIDE THAT CERTAIN ESTABLISHED CHURCHES AND RELIGIOUS ORGANIZATIONS ARE NOT COVERED BY THIS ORDINANCE, AND THAT PERSONS ENGAGED IN CASUAL OR ISOLATED ACTIVITY SUCH AS YARD SALES ARE NOT COVERED BY THIS ORDINANCE; TO PROVIDE FOR THE READOPTION OF ALL OTHER PROVISIONS OF THE OCCUPATIONAL TAX ORDINANCE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.

WHEREAS, the Town Council of the’ Town of Clermont, Georgia, is authorized by Art. IX, § II, { II of the Constitution of the State of Georgia of 1983, to enact ordinances for the health, safety and welfare of the general public; and

WHEREAS, pursuant to 0.C.G.A. §8§ 48-13-1 and 48-13-5, et seq., the Town Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia, adopted an Occupational Tax Ordinance on December 22, 1994 for the Town of Clermont, Georgia; and

WHEREAS, the General Assembly amended the statutes concerning occupational taxes assessed in Georgia, and pursuant to 0.C.G.A. §

48-13-27, requires each entity which assesses occupational taxes to amend its Ordinance to bring said Ordinance into compliance with the laws established by the General Assembly; and

WHEREAS, the Town Council desires to amend said Ordinance to bring the Ordinance into compliance with the statutes as amended by the General Assembly; and

WHEREAS, the Town Council also desires to amend said Ordinance to provide that certain other businesses are not covered by said Ordinance;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Town Council of Clermont, Georgia, and it is hereby ordained by authority of same, as follows:

In addition to the other remedies herein provided for the collection of the occupation tax herein levied, the Mayor, any member of the Council, the Town Clerk, the Town Attorney, or other proper agent of the Town upon any tax or installment of said tax becoming delinquent and remaining unpaid, shall issue execution for the correct amount of said tax against the person liable for said tax, which execution shall bear interest at the rate of one and one-half (1 1/2%) percent per month from the date which such tax or installment becomes delinquent (April 1), and the lien shall cover the property of the person liable for said tax, all as provided by the Ordinances and Charter of the Town and the laws of Georgia. The lien of said occupation tax shall become fixed on and date from the time when such tax or any installment thereof becomes delinquent. The execution shall be levied by the Mayor, any member of the Council, the Town Clerk, the Town Attorney, or other proper agent of the Town, upon the property of the person liable for said tax, and sufficient property shall be advertised and sold to pay the amount of said execution, with interest and costs. All other proceedings in relation thereto shall be had as is provided by the ordinances and the Charter of the Town and the laws of Georgia, and the defendant in said execution shall have rights of defense, by affidavit of illegality and otherwise, which are provided by the

Charter of the Town and the laws of Georgia in regard to tax

executions. When a nulla bona entry has been entered by proper authority upon an execution issued by the Mayor, any member of the Council, the Town Clerk, the Town Attorney, or other proper agent of the Town, against any person defaulting on the occupation tax, the person against whom the entry was made shall not be allowed or entitled to have or collect any fees or charges whatsoever for services rendered after the entry of the nulla bona. If, at any time after the entry of nulla bona has been made, the person against whom the execution issues pays the tax in full together with all interest, penalties and costs accrued on the tax, the person may collect any fees and charges due the person as though the person had never defaulted in the payment of the taxes.
32: All other provisions of the Occupational Tax Ordinance for the Town of Clermont, Georgia, which was duly passed on December 12, 1994, are readopted and reaffirmed, and shall not be effected by this Ordinance.
